Sara: heads up — embedding mismatch on the new reranker after HF->Redwood conversion. mean pooling on HF vs CLS on Redwood? numbers are off by ~0.35 cosine for some queries :thinking:
Omar: can you paste the tokenizer/config + convert command you used? might be a mapping issue with special tokens or truncation strategy
Sara: here's the convert command and the config snippet i used
```bash
python convert_hf_to_redwood.py \
  --model-dir ./hf-model \
  --out ./redwood-model --force-tokenizer-mapping
```
```json
{"tokenizer_class": "ByteLevelBPETokenizer", "add_prefix_space": true, "special_tokens_map": {"cls_token": "<s>", "sep_token": "</s>"}, "pad_token_id": 1}
```
Li: quick thought — HF repo we started from used a CLS token physically present at index 0 and embeddings training used that. The default embeddings pooling in Redwood runtime might be using mean pooling excluding special tokens unless `pooling_strategy` set. See: `pooling_strategy: cls_token` vs `mean_last`.
Eva: can you dump token ids for a failing example? want to confirm where truncation is chopping context. default HF truncation was `longest_first` with stride=0, while Redwood conversion tool set `truncation_side: "left"` for some reason.
Sara: example text -> token ids (HF vs Redwood after convert):
HF: [0, 57, 348, 1299, 2, 1, 1]
Redwood: [57, 348, 1299, 2, 1]
Omar: aha — looks like the leading CLS (<s>) got dropped during conversion so CLS pooling on Redwood had nothing to pool. That explains the lower similarity when our reranker expects CLS.
Li: also check `special_tokens_map` vs `added_tokens`. convert script may set `cls_token` name but not inject it into `added_tokens` so tokenizer never prepends it.
Eva: small script to force consistent behavior:
```python
# force cls pooling and ensure token present before encoding
tokenizer.add_tokens([tokenizer.cls_token])
inputs = tokenizer(text, truncation=True, max_length=256, padding='max_length', return_tensors='pt')
embeds = model(**inputs).last_hidden_state
cls_emb = embeds[:, 0, :]
```
Sara: nice. i also noticed Redwood runtime default for embeddings truncation was `truncate_right` which shifts context compared to HF's `truncate_left` for our pairwise setup — that changes local token windows and scores.
Omar: proposed fix: update convert tool to copy `tokenizer.json` fields exactly and add explicit `pooling_strategy` metadata into `config.json` for embeddings endpoints. Then run A/B on the reranker.
Sara: i can run a quick ablation: 1) add cls token to tokenizer, 2) set pooling_strategy=cls, 3) set truncation_side=right/left variants. will post results.
bench-bot: scheduled reranker-emb-compare job: job/47821 started (params: pooling=cls, trunc_side=left) :rocket:
Li: FYI for future models we should assert roundtrip invariants in CI: token ids for a canonical sentence, presence of special tokens, and explicit pooling key in config.json.
Eva: also log the `token_type_ids` — some HF models used token_type to encode role; if conversion drops those, mean vs cls can diverge.
Sara: thanks all. i'll update the conversion PR with the tests and a toggle to force `pooling_strategy` for embeddings endpoints. ping me if you want to help run the dataset-level reruns.
Omar: thanks — will take the follow-up for integrating into the infra job (eng-ml infra ticket: https://redwood-internal/issue/ML-3421) :eyes:
